dedupe_keys.name: greenmove park visitation network for shanghai from mobile phone data 2014

description: GreenMove is a bipartite dynamic mobility network linking residential areas to parks in Shanghai, built from telecom operator records of about 10 million anonymised mobile phone users between January and April 2014. Stays were clustered and classified as home, work or other, and other stays overlapping parks were counted as park visits; the metropolitan area is divided into 38,055 cell-tower Voronoi residential polygons. The release has 113 daily networks and 452 intra-day segmented networks, a four-month super-network, and a CSV for a gradient boosting model of pairwise flows; edges carry flow, commuter ratio and distance, and nodes carry socioeconomic and weather attributes. Coverage: Shanghai, 1 January to 29 April 2014, with 3 February and 12 to 16 February omitted. Access: free Figshare download with code on GitHub. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: raw phone data and the visit-detection code are not public, and winter to spring months only. Simulation uses: park demand and catchment models, and flows to green space under heat or closures. Related records: the OpenSpaceGlobal megacity open space data and the large public urban green space indicators.
